item.title: Brown out of NI Open after Donaldson defeat
item.description: Donaldson will now face Jones in the last 16 [Getty Images] Scott Donaldson ended a six-year wait for a ranking quarter-final appearance with a 4-2 win over Antrim native Jordan Brown at the Northern Ireland Open. The world number 64 edged ahead three times during a cagey encounter before securing the final frame to book his place in the last eight at the Waterfront Hall. Donaldson won the opening frame in a tight start, but Brown levelled before the Scot won the next two frames to move to within one of victory. Brown responded again in the fifth to keep the contest alive, but Donaldson held his nerve to secure his first ranking quarter-final since the 2020 Northern Ireland Open. "I get more enjoyment out of the playing aspect of the game, so it wasn't totally enjoyable tonight," Donaldson told BBC Sport NI. "I got myself through to the next round and that is all really that matters but, obviously, playing Jordan is hard and then the table was really, really tough as the pockets were so tight. "This combined with the fact that I'm not overly confident right now. I'm OK in patches but just all that made for a tough evening." Elsewhere, Jak Jones held off a late fightback from Daniel Wells to progress with a 4-2 win. Three-time world champion Mark Williams produced a commanding display to beat Martin O'Donnell 4-0, compiling breaks of 58 and 127 to reach the last eight. David Gilbert also advanced with a win over Kai Wai Cheung, who had beaten Ronnie O'Sullivan in the first round. In Thursday's earlier session, Kyren Wilson won a final-frame decider against Junxu Pang as he continues his quest for his first ranking win since his Players Championship win over Judd Trump in March 2025. Quarter-final draw - Friday 23 October From 13:00 BST Anthony McGill v Kyren Wilson Sam Craigie v Elliot Slessor David Gilbert v Mark Williams Jak Jones v Scott Donaldson

item.title: Drama In the Aspar Moto2 Garage
item.description: "No relationship whatsoever" between teammates Alonso and Holgado MotoGP has seen several high-profile rivalries between teammates over the years, and we now have the makings for some animosity within the Aspar Moto2 garage. Speaking with Spanish broadcaster DAZN, CFMOTO Power Electronics Aspar rider David Alonso made clear he is not on speaking terms with teammate Dani Holgado after his role in causing the crash that ended Alonso's race at the Indonesian Grand Prix. The flashpoint came at Turn 1 in Mandalika, where Holgado made contact with the rear of Alonso's Kalex braking into the corner and knocked him into a violent highside. Alonso's #80 bike was damaged badly enough to require repairs back in the Aspar box, which kept him from rejoining once the race was red-flagged and restarted. He also walked away with a pulmonary contusion. Holgado, who caused the incident, drew no penalty from the stewards, suffered no injury, and rejoined from his original grid slot to finish third behind Izan Guevara and Manu Gonzalez. The result allowed Holgado to leapfrog Alonso in the standings, putting him fourth overall and just 4 points ahead of his teammate. This was not the first collision between the two. They were weekend-to-weekend rivals in Moto3, and Holgado ran into the back of Alonso at Jerez last year. For Alonso, Mandalika was the last straw. "Life is good, and you have to keep moving forward. When someone is not a good person, there's nothing you can do. I'm doing my thing, and he's doing his," Alonso said. "There's no relationship whatsoever, there's no chemistry in the team, and it's not a team. The incident is the least of it." "There's much more to it than that; I'm simply carrying on my way - there's no point wasting time on people who aren't worth it." For his part, Holgado took ownership of his role in the crash after the Mandalika race, saying: "I'd like to apologise for what happened, both to my teammate David Alonso and to the team. These things sometimes happen in the first few corners, but I'm not using that as an excuse and I take full responsibility for my mistake." At Phillip Island, when DAZN asked him about Alonso's comments, Holgado said he'd like to clear the air, but understands how his teammate may feel "in the heat of the moment". "It's normal; we've only been in Australia for two days and we haven't discussed the matter. I'd like to discuss it, because I've got no problem with it, and I think we're old enough to talk about these things," Holgado said. "But anyway, I'm sure we'll talk about it in the future. I'm not letting it bother me; these things happen – it's pure and simple rivalry, and that's part of the sport." No matter what their relationship, Holgado and Alonso will only remain teammates for another few rounds. Both riders are headed to MotoGP in 2027, but on separate teams - Alonso to LCR Honda on a factory contract and Holgado to Gresini Ducati - and can continue their rivalry in the premier class. The Bruins (7-2-1) will look to launch a new winning streak as they return home to host the Predators (3-2-3) on Thursday. Boston's five-game winning streak came to an end after the Bruins suffered a 3-2 overtime loss to the Stars on Tuesday. Matthew Poitras and James Hagens found the back of the net for Boston, but Mikko Rantanen scored three times, including the overtime winner on the power play. The Predators will head to Boston following a four-day break. They defeated the Blues, 5-2, on Saturday. NESN provided live coverage of Thursday's game between the Bruins and Predators. item.title: LeBron James and Joel Embiid already have a viral moment with the 76ers
item.description: LeBron James and Joel Embiid already have a viral moment with the 76ers originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . There's a new player in Philadelphia, and you may have heard of him. LeBron James debuted with the Philadelphia 76ers this week, so far, and it's brought the drama and viral moments that fans hoped it would bring. The 76ers pulled off a win over the reigning champions, the New York Knicks , on Tuesday in a 106-100 victory to kick off the season. As sweet as that win was for Philly, seeing the bond forming between James and the team's other blockbuster star, Joel Embiid, may be even sweeter. LeBron James and Joel Embiid's hilarious handshake has fans talking after the 76ers' home opener James has only been playing with the 76ers for a few days, but he already has a viral handshake with Embiid. This handshake is really getting attention on Thursday, during the team's home opener against the Cleveland Cavaliers . The new power couple showed off this special handshake on the court before the 76ers-Cavs game, and it's a funny exchange that involves the two slapping their hands against each other and moving in a wiggle dance move that you have to see to believe. ESPN's NBA account shared the moment on X , formerly Twitter, on Thursday, and within a few hours, it racked up more than 600,000 views. That's really the power of putting James with a famed player like Embiid, and it's perhaps a sign of things to come. Bron's new handshake with Embiid 😂😭 https://t.co/MgepjSJTe4 — NBA on ESPN (@ESPNNBA) October 22, 2026 "City of brotherly love," one follower said on X in reaction. "That handshake has more moves than most playoff offenses, and I respect the commitment to the bit," another said. "Bron got a new handshake for every teammate. The chemistry is hilarious, and Embiid is matching the energy," one more said. So, the fans are loving this handshake. Even if it's a bit eccentric, that's really the point, and these two appear totally into it. More NBA news: Lakers get major Bronny James update before season opener vs. Warriors Detroit's J.B. item.title: Kentucky Basketball pursued Akron transfer Amani Lyles before Cincinnati commitment
item.description: Kentucky Basketball was apparently making a push for Akron transfer small forward Amani Lyles before he committed to Cincinnati on Thursday, according to Joe Tipton of On3. Lyles, who stands 6-foot-7 and weighs 226 pounds, spent all four of his collegiate seasons at Akron before entering the transfer portal. He committed to Cincinnati in hopes of playing a fifth season while navigating the eligibility questions surrounding ongoing court cases. According to Jack Pilgrim of KSR, uncertainty about whether Lyles would be eligible to play this season was one of the main reasons Kentucky backed off. Pilgrim also reported that Cincinnati believed Lyles was destined to commit to Kentucky, but Lyles didn’t want to wait to decide, ultimately leading him to become a Bearcat. Lyles is coming off the best season of his collegiate career, averaging 14.9 points, 7.9 rebounds, 2.2 assists, 1.0 steals and 0.7 blocks per game while shooting 55.8% from the field. He also shot 37.3% from 3-point range on 3.6 attempts per game, making him a potential stretch 4 option who could have fit well into Mark Pope’s lineup at Kentucky. Pope still has one roster spot available, and it will be interesting to see whether he fills it before the season begins. With the season less than two weeks away, however, the Wildcats have little time to add another player.

item.title: Live Coverage: Drake Maye gets the Patriots on the board, back in the game vs. Bears
item.description: The New England Patriots make a quick return to the field Thursday night as they look to win their fourth straight game in primetime against the Chicago Bears. Drake Maye will have several backup offensive linemen protecting him as a spate of injuries has left the Patriots without Ben Brown and Alijah Vera-Tucker. New England had already seen injuries to right guard Michael Onwenu and top backup guard Greg Van Roten, placing both of them on the injured reserve. SECOND QUARTER UPDATES 2:09 — Another penalty by the Patriots. Gabe Jacas with a late hit on Caleb Williams. 2:50 — The Patriots defense appears to bail out the offense and force the Bears to three-and-out. But Charles Woods is called for holding and it’s first down. 3:25 — Brutal. Drake Maye is intercepted in the end zone. 4:10 — Drake Maye gets 10 yards and then some as he moves the Patriots down the field. 6:48 — Efton Chism’s first grab of the night gets the Patriots a first down with a 16-yard catch-and-run. INJURY UPDATE: SCORE UPDATE: Bears 13, Patriots 7 7:04 — Three more for Chicago after another field goal. 7:30 — That’s a new one. item.title: Dawn Staley says Final Four spat with Geno Auriemma was about more than a handshake
item.description: College Basketball: NCAA Final Four: UConn Head Coach Geno Auriemma and South Carolina Head Coach Dawn Staley ague during the game at Mortgage Matchup Center. Phoenix, AZ 4/3/2026 CREDIT: Jordan Murph (Photo by Jordan Murph/Sports Illustrated via Getty Images) (Set Number: X164875 TK1) (Jordan Murph/Sports Illustrated via Getty Ima) Dawn Staley came out to raucous applause at South Carolina's Garnet and Black Madness event Wednesday, marking the customary start of a new Gamecocks basketball season. However, the South Carolina coach isn't quite ready to let go of last season, particularly her memorable Final Four clash with UConn women's basketball coach and longtime rival Geno Auriemma six months ago. Staley appeared on the Grey Matter with Declan Kelly podcast Wednesday, offering her perspective on the heated confrontation between the two Hall of Fame coaches. "I'm going to speak about it right now because I haven't talked about it," Staley said. "I think Geno really thinks it's about the handshake, and it has very little to do with the handshake. I respect him. I respect what he's done for the game. I think he's a genius of a coach." "Understand this: when we played UConn, whether I was at Temple or at South Carolina, and they were the overarching favorites and beat us by 20, 30, 40 points, I made a point to always, after the game, shake his hand, look him in his eye, congratulate him and move on. I did it purposefully; I made myself do that." Tensions at the blue-blooded Final Four matchup boiled over by the end of the third quarter, as Auriemma gave an irate interview to Holly Rowe with his UConn squad trailing by five, railing against an officiating crew that hadn't whistled a foul against South Carolina since the first half. South Carolina pulled away for a 62-48 win, and Auriemma set off Staley in the postgame handshake line, leading to a heated confrontation that led to the coaches being separated. Auriemma said in his postgame interview that he felt snubbed by Staley, alleging that the South Carolina coach left him waiting for a customary pregame handshake. After widespread criticism from national media figures and former players, Auriemma issued an apology statement to Staley. Staley, meanwhile, largely glossed over the incident and expressed frustration that the controversy overshadowed her team's accomplishment. South Carolina then lost to UCLA 79-51 in the national championship game two days later. Sign up for the Connecticut Briefing from CT Insider. Get the biggest headlines of the day from our network of journalists around the state. This article originally published at Dawn Staley says Final Four spat with Geno Auriemma was about more than a handshake .

item.title: Thursday’s LSU vs. Auburn injury report: Trey’Dez Green not listed
item.description: OXFORD, MISSISSIPPI - SEPTEMBER 19: Trey'Dez Green #7 and head coach Lane Kiffin of the LSU Tigers in action against the Ole Miss Rebels at Vaught Hemingway Stadium on September 19, 2026 in Oxford, Mississippi. (Photo by Gus Stark/LSU/University Images via Getty Images) The second injury report is out for LSU vs Auburn in Jordan-Hare Stadium this Saturday. Kickoff is for 11 am central. The biggest news is the removal of Trey’Dez Green. This is something to monitor throughout the week to see if he pops back up based on his potential return to practice, but it appears as if the Tigers could be getting their star tight end back earlier than they anticipated. Princewill Umanmielen and Jackson Harris both not being listed on the injury report is important to note, as well. Both left the game early against Mississippi St last week, but appear to be back healthy and ready to go. LSU Out LB #7 Whit Weeks S #10 Dashawn Spears WR #15 Phillip Wright III LB #26 Charles Ross II DT #88 Richard Anderson Although not officially confirmed, it appears that Richard Anderson is not traveling with the team due to personal/family matters and is not injured. Auburn Out OL #71 Tai Buster TE #85 Hunter Herring Questionable DL #99 Saint Farrior

item.title: Three Goals for #3 Ohio State as Women’s Soccer Falls 3-0 in Columbus
item.description: COLUMBUS, Ohio — Ohio State came into Thursday night having allowed seven goals in 14 matches, the fewest in the Big Ten. Rutgers did not put a shot on target until the 53rd minute. The third-ranked Buckeyes beat the Scarlet Knights 3-0 at Jesse Owens Memorial Stadium. Ava Bramblett scored at 3:12. Callie Tumilty came off the bench at 22:40 and scored at 25:17, then came back on at 75:04 and added a second at 82:09. Ohio State outshot Rutgers 28-9 and put seven on target to two, Peighton Northrup needed two saves for the clean sheet, and Olivia Bodmer made four at the other end. Three goals for the No. 3 team in the country. It is the third straight match in which Rutgers has not scored, 270 minutes of soccer since the 3-2 win over Northwestern on Oct. 8, after a 0-0 draw with Nebraska and Saturday’s 1-0 loss on a penalty at Penn State. It is also the first time since the opener at Tennessee that Rutgers has lost by more than a goal. Five of the six losses before Thursday came by one. Thursday was not close. Ohio State arrived 12-1-1 and 8-1-0, alone at the top of the Big Ten and third in both the coaches poll and the RPI. The No. 3 ranking is the highest in program history, and nine straight weeks in the top 10 is the longest run the Buckeyes have had. Their only loss came 1-0 to UCLA in September, the same scoreline UCLA beat Rutgers by at Yurcak. On Sunday they won 2-1 at No. 20 Purdue, where Nette-Nina Hiltunen headed in a free kick delivered by Bramblett at 6:06, Jaiden Anderson equalized at 19:58 and Elle Britt scored at 47:30 off an Amanda Schlueter pass. Sophomore Lizzie Rozmajzl, making her first career start in goal, saved Anderson’s penalty in the 71st minute. Lori Walker-Hock’s side is built from the back. Northrup came in leading the Big Ten in goals-against average at 0.47 and in save percentage at .872. Last season the Buckeyes went 11-5-6 and reached the program’s third Elite Eight, and nine starters came back from that team. Ohio State had never beaten Rutgers before last year. It has now done it twice in a row. Lineup GK : Olivia Bodmer D : Julia Joseph, Lindsey Hailey, Morgan Hippeli, Riley Morris, Patricia Tsokos M : Tommi Valente F : Lilia Calvert, Reilly McGlinn, Ashley Baran, Marian Dunne Subs : Sophia Stiles, Bea Tinoco, Olivia Russomanno, Audrey Cain, Jayme Malanda, Sarah Martinez, Amanda Thornton, Emma Johns Mike O’Neill made one change to the eleven that started at Penn State, with Riley Morris in for Audrey Cain. Gabriela Gil did not appear for a second straight match, and neither did Dina Bojkovic, Lily Ann Phillips or Charlotte Garcia, all of whom played at Jeffrey Field. The count landed exactly where it did against Purdue in September, with 25 changes, eight substitutes and 19 players. The first half went in four waves. Sarah Martinez and Sophia Stiles replaced Morris and Hippeli at 23:55, 82 seconds before Ohio State’s second goal. Amanda Thornton replaced Marian Dunne at 28:24, Olivia Russomanno and Jayme Malanda
item.content:encoded: COLUMBUS, Ohio — Ohio State came into Thursday night having allowed seven goals in 14 matches, the fewest in the Big Ten. Rutgers did not put a shot on target until the 53rd minute. The third-ranked Buckeyes beat the Scarlet Knights 3-0 at Jesse Owens Memorial Stadium. Ava Bramblett scored at 3:12. Sophomore Lizzie Rozmajzl, making her first career start in goal, saved Anderson’s penalty in the 71st minute. Lori Walker-Hock’s side is built from the back. Northrup came in leading the Big Ten in goals-against average at 0.47 and in save percentage at .872. Last season the Buckeyes went 11-5-6 and reached the program’s third Elite Eight, and nine starters came back from that team. Ohio State had never beaten Rutgers before last year. It has now done it twice in a row. Lineup GK : Olivia Bodmer D : Julia Joseph, Lindsey Hailey, Morgan Hippeli, Riley Morris, Patricia Tsokos M : Tommi Valente F : Lilia Calvert, Reilly McGlinn, Ashley Baran, Marian Dunne Subs : Sophia Stiles, Bea Tinoco, Olivia Russomanno, Audrey Cain, Jayme Malanda, Sarah Martinez, Amanda Thornton, Emma Johns Mike O’Neill made one change to the eleven that started at Penn State, with Riley Morris in for Audrey Cain. Gabriela Gil did not appear for a second straight match, and neither did Dina Bojkovic, Lily Ann Phillips or Charlotte Garcia, all of whom played at Jeffrey Field. The count landed exactly where it did against Purdue in September, with 25 changes, eight substitutes and 19 players. The first half went in four waves. Sarah Martinez and Sophia Stiles replaced Morris and Hippeli at 23:55, 82 seconds before Ohio State’s second goal. Amanda Thornton replaced Marian Dunne at 28:24, Olivia Russomanno and Jayme Malanda replaced Baran and McGlinn at 30:42, and Johns and Cain replaced Valente and Calvert at 38:17. From there to the break, Bodmer, Joseph, Hailey and Tsokos were the only starters on the field. What changed was the interval. For four straight matches the Rutgers coach had restored his starting eleven in full at 45:00. On Thursday he brought back four, Dunne, Valente, Calvert and Baran, and left Stiles, Thornton and Malanda on. Morris never returned after her 24 minutes. Hippeli came back at 59:29, and McGlinn, who led both teams with five shots at Penn State, came back at 63:37 and finished with 49 minutes and no shots. Fourteen more changes followed after halftime, four of them at once at 74:29. Cain and Russomanno lasted 3 minutes and 28 seconds of that wave before Valente and Calvert came back on for them at 77:57. Thornton went on at 28:24 and never came off, 61 minutes in one shift. Tsokos came off at 83:09, and the four who had gone the full 90 at Penn State became two. Bodmer and Hailey were the only Scarlet Knights to play all 90. Bramblett Scores in Three, and Rutgers Waits Another Forty to Shoot Ohio State outshot Rutgers 16-1 in the first half and put four on target to none. It won four corners to none. Rutgers committed three fouls to Ohio State’s one and was flagged offside once. There were no cards. Bodmer made two saves. Northrup made none. Ava Greco was called for a foul at 1:17, the only foul Ohio State committed all half. At 2:39 the Buckeyes won their first corner, and 33 seconds later Bramblett scored off assists from Greco and Andrea Lu to make it 1-0. Bramblett, filed as a defender in the box score, had also opened the scoring in the fifth minute against Northwestern on Oct. 3. Ohio State won another corner at 4:45, and Hiltunen put one over the top at 5:23. Schlueter’s attempt at 7:04 did not reach Bodmer, Lu went wide left four seconds later and Jadin Bonham tried again at 7:55. After another corner at 8:09, Britt sent one over the top left at 8:36, and at 9:27 Bodmer made her first save, on a Bonham shot struck high. That was six Ohio State shots in four minutes and four seconds. Morris was called for a foul at 11:01. Schlueter went at Bodmer again at 15:02, Ohio State won a corner at 15:45, and at 16:48 Schlueter hit the crossbar. McGlinn fouled at 18:25, and Schlueter went over the top at 22:31. Walker-Hock made her first change nine seconds later, sending Tumilty on for Bonham at 22:40. Lu’s attempt at 23:50 did not reach the goal, O’Neill made his first two changes at 23:55, and at 25:17 Tumilty scored off assists from Britt and Lu to make it 2-0. She had been on the field for 2 minutes and 37 seconds. Both benches made five more changes in the next 15 minutes, and the match settled down without becoming any more even. Mia Stevens forced Bodmer’s second save at 31:49, again high. Schlueter went off at 33:30 for Riley Lijewski, and Britt and Tumilty missed over the top right and wide left 20 seconds apart, at 40:30 and 40:50. Rutgers was flagged offside at 41:32. At 43:20 Russomanno took Rutgers’ first shot of the night, and it did not reach Northrup. Lijewski sent Ohio State’s 16th attempt wide right at 44:25. A year ago at Yurcak, Ohio State led this fixture 3-0 at halftime. This time it was two, and the gap did not feel any smaller. Rutgers went to the break with one shot, none on target and no corners. Rutgers Finds the Frame Twice, and Tumilty Comes Back On to Finish It Rutgers was better after the break, which was not a high bar. Dunne was booked at 45:21, 21 seconds after coming back on. Ohio State won a corner at 47:54, and at 52:32 Baran put Rutgers’ first shot on target of the night at Northrup, bottom center, for a save. Stiles was booked 28 seconds later. Then came the best stretch Rutgers had all night. After Lu went over the top at 54:52, Valente’s shot at 55:38 did not reach Northrup, and Rutgers won corners at 55:41 and 56:14. Hailey went over the top at 56:33, and Joseph’s attempt at 57:13 did not reach the goal either. Three shots and two corners in 95 seconds, and nothing for Northrup to handle. Ohio State answered at the other end. Schlueter shot at 57:33, the Buckeyes won a corner four seconds later, and at 59:26 Schlueter put her only shot on target of the night at Bodmer, high, for a save. Walker-Hock brought Bonham back on for Tumilty three seconds later, and O’Neill sent Hippeli back on for Joseph on the same stoppage. Joseph and McGlinn returned at 63:37, Mia McSweeney went over the top at 64:25, and Tinoco and Martinez came on at 67:26. Thornton was booked at 69:47, and Bonham went over the top at 71:02. At 74:00 Britt hit the left post. Four seconds later Schlueter went over the top. O’Neill made his four changes at 74:29, Walker-Hock sent Tumilty back on for McSweeney at 75:04, and Tsokos fouled at 77:03. At 77:14 Bramblett went top left and Bodmer saved it. It was the last save Bodmer made. Russomanno went wide right at

item.title: Baker Mayfield’s Glove And Grit Are Ready For Panthers Showdown
item.description: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images Baker Mayfield is expected to start for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers this Sunday against the Carolina Panthers. ESPN reports he has practiced fully after missing three weeks with a dislocated right thumb. The team sits at 1-5, making this game a must-win for their season. He will wear a special glove with metal reinforcement to protect his hand. A Metal Reinforcement For A Broken Thumb The equipment staff got creative to help him. They reached out to the Tampa Bay Rays for advice on how to build a protective pad. The final result is a glove with a pad on the back of the thumb and metal inside to stop it from bending backward. It sounds like a lot of extra gear, but Mayfield says it feels natural. He told reporters on Thursday that the adjustment was the hard part. “It’s just like me wearing a glove,” he said. The big worry was the impact of the ball when he snaps it from under center. That contact used to scare him, but now he says, “It feels fine gripping it, throwing it.” When a player trusts his hands again, the whole offense starts to breathe easier. His rookie backup, Jalon Daniels, played well enough to win one game against Dallas. But the Bucs need their veteran leader back. Mayfield has not missed a start since joining the team in 2023. He signed a massive $165 million contract extension before this season started. That money is on the line, and so is the pride of a franchise that has lost five games. Why The Bucs Must Fix Their Mistakes Now This team is in a deep hole. They are last in the NFC South with a 3-2 Carolina team waiting for them. Mayfield admits the team has been overthinking things. “We weren’t doing the little things right,” he said. He does not think his teammates are dumb, but they are hesitating when they should be moving fast. The numbers show a team that has struggled. Mayfield has thrown two touchdowns and two interceptions while losing three fumbles. He has been sacked 13 times. The offensive line is playing better now, but they need to stay on the same page with the quarterback. “You need to understand that you build this system based on timing,” Mayfield explained. He knows the injury was painful. “Anytime you dislocate something there’s gonna be ligament damage,” he said. The surgery I required was not for ligaments and tendons, as it just so happened. He is back because he believes his hand is “strong enough to be able to play.” That confidence is what the fans need to see on Sunday. The Bucs wasted a 16-3 lead in their loss to Pittsburgh and lost in overtime. They cannot let that happen again. With Mayfield back, the team has a chance to stop the bleeding. He has played through pain before in his career, starting with his time in Cleveland. He knows what it takes to win when things are tough. The metal glove might look strange, but it is the sign of a fighter who refuses to stay on the bench.

The Bucs wasted a 16-3 lead in their loss to Pittsburgh and lost in overtime. They cannot let that happen again. With Mayfield back, the team has a chance to stop the bleeding. He has played through pain before in his career, starting with his time in Cleveland. He knows what it takes to win when things are tough. The metal glove might look strange, but it is the sign of a fighter who refuses to stay on the bench.

item.title: Marshall Faulk publicly discloses Parkinson’s diagnosis: ‘I’m in a good place’
item.description: Credit: Kirby Lee-USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Connect This summer, Ahman Green, the Green Bay Packers’ all-time leading rusher, disclosed his early-onset Parkinson’s disease diagnosis while appearing on Tyler Dunne’s “Go Long” podcast , and former Tennessee Titans star running back Chris Johnson revealed his ALS diagnosis to Michael Strahan on Good Morning America . Marshall Faulk observed the media coverage of his retired NFL brethren and felt compelled to share his own Parkinson’s diagnosis. “I’m one of the lucky ones,” Faulk said on “ The Caring Neurologist ” with Dr. Sandeep Thakkar. “I spoke with a couple of guys who played NFL ball, and they told me about some of the symptoms and things that they had that they thought was just football-related — that it didn’t relate to Parkinson’s in any manner. They wish, in those early stages, if they would have maybe just knew a little earlier that they would be in better shape. As I started to do my research, realizing that the earlier you catch it, the better chance you have at living a better quality of life.” Faulk, 53, said that his goal is to “help as many people as I can” by sharing his story. The Pro Football Hall of Fame inductee said he first noticed rigidity in his hand while playing golf, which he initially dismissed as “normal nerves when putting and stuff like that.” At one of his regular physicals, Faulk told his doctor he’d experienced hand symptoms outside of golf. Faulk’s doctor implored him “to go get checked,” leading to the diagnosis. “In any phase of life, whenever you break through a barrier or you find some things out, what you want to do with that information is pass it on to the next generation to make sure that they have it better — that they know more,” Faulk said. “And you’re doing the ‘leave this world in a better place than it was when I got here.’ That’s what we want to do. So, in this case, it’s no different.” “I continue to mentor and coach young men now,” Faulk added. “I helped young guys come into the NFL and transition from college. This falls into the same arena with guys that’s going to be retiring. Whether you have the little tremors in your hand or you start to get the rigidity, and you’re like, ‘Oh, it’s arthritis.’ And then, you hear it might not be; it could be something else. Like I did, you go get checked, and you go find out.” Faulk relayed his mindset as taking solace in Parkinson’s diagnosis not being “something that’s terminal,” and he plans to learn to live with it. “I haven’t had many episodes,” Faulk said, noting. “I appear to be fine.” After starring for the Indianapolis Colts and the then-St. Louis Rams from 1994 to 2005, Faulk retired from the NFL in March 2007. By November, Faulk joined NFL Network as an analyst. In 2017, NFL Network suspended Faulk , Ike Taylor, and Heath Evans in the wake of a sexual harassment lawsuit, effectively ending Faulk’s tenure . Faulk is now the head coach at Southern University . The post Marshall Faulk publicly disc

item.title: UTSA-Tulane football: How to watch as Roadrunners brace for another tight battle
item.description: UTSA Roadrunner Will Henderson shakes tackles as he runs for a touchdown against Navy at the Alamodome, Saturday, October 17, 2026. (Cody Duty/Contributor) Falling into a 14-0 hole for the second time this season, UTSA quarterback Owen McCown already knew what to expect. And when the time came to deliver a game-winning drive late in the fourth quarter, McCown was prepared to meet that moment, too. All five of the Roadrunners' games against Group of Six opponents this year have been played within a one-score margin at some point during the final quarter, and all five have ended with wins. McCown's third late game-winning drive of the season lifted UTSA to a 38-34 victory over Navy on Saturday in the Alamodome, pushing the Roadrunners to 6-1 overall and 3-0 in the American Conference. "The guys don't really blink. We don't really look at the score," McCown said. "We just know we've got to go out and execute the next play, and that's what we did." READ MORE: After heart procedure, UTSA corner RJ Lester finds new joy in football With UTSA listed as just a 3-point favorite entering a matchup with Tulane at 7 p.m. Saturday at Yulman Stadium in New Orleans, the Roadrunners are bracing for another tight finish in what coach Jeff Traylor warns will be a season full of them. Traylor said the Roadrunners trust a more healthy McCown to deliver in those moments with both his arm and legs this year, and offensive linemen Ben Rios said UTSA's front is confident in McCown's ability to come through as long as they can hold up in protection. "Owen has been doing a good job compared to the last couple years with game-winning drives," Rios said. "I think he's really just stepped up his game, and he's more confident back there, and he's leading the ship." UTSA vs. Tulane: 5 players to watch as Roadrunners aim to keep rolling How to watch UTSA at Tulane Matchup: UTSA (6-1, 3-0 American) at Tulane (3-3, 1-1) When: 7 p.m. Saturday Where: Yulman Stadium, New Orleans TV: ESPNU Radio: 760 AM All-time series: UTSA leads 2-1 Last meeting: UTSA won 48-26 on Oct. 30, 2025, in San Antonio Last game: UTSA won 38-34 against Navy on Oct. 17 in San Antonio; Tulane won 31-17 against Memphis on Oct. 16 in New Orleans READ MORE: How UTSA's Brandon Young delivered on long-awaited opportunity Subscribe There’s more to San Antonio with the Express-News. item.title: “Rooks Are Not Allowed to Speak”: Eddie Johnson Slams Warriors Rookie Yaxel Lendeborg for Taking Shots at Luka Doncic After One Game
item.description: Yaxel Lendeborg and Luka Doncic © Instagram/@yaxellendeborg, X/@Lakers Golden State Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg wasted no time making headlines after his NBA debut on Wednesday, but it wasn’t just his performance on the court that got people talking. The rookie sparked a debate after accusing Luka Doncic of foul-baiting and constantly complaining to referees. Lendeborg expressed frustration with what he witnessed, saying he had “lost respect” after watching Doncic repeatedly “whining” to officials. His comments clearly ruffled a few feathers, even drawing the ire of former NBA player and broadcaster Eddie Johnson. On Thursday on X, Johnson unloaded on the rookie for criticizing established stars after playing just one professional game. “Rooks are not allowed to speak, especially one that says he never watched the NBA growing up,” Johnson wrote on X. “Did Draymond take this kid in a room and pull a Phil Jackson with some incense and hallucinatory babble? Rookie breaking down Luka like he been around for years! Be quiet and be a rookie and learn. This rant after one game is unreal!” While Eddie Johnson’s old school expectations may have worked in his era, the NBA has changed a lot since then. Today’s players grow up in a different media world, and Lendeborg is no exception. Lendeborg has already shown that he is funny, blunt and unafraid to speak his mind. But at the same time, he proved he can play. Being trusted as a starter on a fading Warriors dynasty speaks volumes about his potential. In his first assignment guarding Doncic, a six-time All-Star and perennial MVP candidate, Lendeborg held his own defensively. The Lakers guard shot just 1 of 6 (16.7%) when guarded by the former Michigan standout. Although the Warriors fell 127-105, the rookie showed flashes of his potential. He finished with 12 points, three rebounds and two assists in 29 minutes in his NBA debut. Warriors Coach Steve Kerr Loves What Yaxel Lendeborg Brings to the Table Warriors coach Steve Kerr has already embraced Yaxel Lendeborg’s outspoken personality. Ever since being drafted, Lendeborg has shown he’s willing to do whatever it takes to learn and earn his spot, and it’s been going well so far. Fans love that kind of attitude. Earlier in the preseason, Kerr also praised Lendeborg’s personality: “You can also see his youth with his comments in the media,” Kerr said, per Anthony Slater. “Our fans are going to love listening to him, and he’s going to say some stuff that he may have to retract and hold back. But I love it. I love him. I love guys like that. We always encourage everyone to be themselves, and he’s got a really great personality.” It’s great when you have the support of your coach and teammates to do and say what you want. While Lendeborg’s comments following the season opener may have raised a few eyebrows, they were refreshing nonetheless. Golden State clearly has big hopes for the rookie, who has shown an NBA readiness that not many expected so soon. At 24,

item.title: Maryland women’s soccer holds on for 1-1 draw against No. 24 Michigan
item.description: The University of Maryland Women’s Soccer Team was defeated by The University of Iowa 1-3 at Ludwig Field on October 16th 2026. | Jessie Reider/Testudo Times In the 62nd minute, Maryland women’s soccer made a goalkeeper change, taking out Faith Luckey and subbing Meredith Fisher into the game. Luckey had made a season-high nine saves to keep the Terps in the game against an onslaught by Michigan’s attack. Just two minutes after the change, Melisa Kekic fired a shot towards Fisher, who misplayed the shot as the ball deflected off her glove and into the back of the net. However, with Luckey out of the game, the luck did not run out for Maryland. A 67th-minute Paige Foye free kick was misplayed by Wolverines netminder Malia Zillman. The ball rolled slowly into the net to bring the score level, helping the Terps secure a 1-1 draw against Michigan. The Terps’ offense struggled throughout the night and could not maintain pressure on the Wolverines’ backline. Maryland had just seven shots throughout the contest, with only two on frame. Maryland’s first opportunity came in the ninth minute, with Jolie Farmer receiving a long pass into Michigan territory, but the ball was cleared out for a corner kick. The Terps couldn’t capitalize as the Wolverines blocked Mckinley Heaven’s shot. While the Terps had just one shot in the first 20 minutes of play, Michigan’s offense also didn’t create major opportunities early, logging three off-target shots of its own over that span. However, as the frame wore on, Michigan found its rhythm on attack. The Wolverines’ first shot on goal came in the 22nd minute, but Ella Jablinsky fired it right to Luckey, who made the easy save. Jablinsky was the primary producer in Michigan’s attack. She attempted four shots in the first half. In the 27th minute, Brooklyn Marn was the first Wolverine to test Luckey on a shot, but the goalkeeper was up to the task and made the diving stop. Michigan’s newfound attacking pressure continued, but Luckey was up to the challenge. She made consecutive saves on shots in the 29th minute to keep the Terps from falling behind early. Luckey made six first-half saves, including multiple diving stops. The Wolverines attempted 11 shots in the first half, but couldn’t beat Luckey on any of them. It took until the 42nd minute for Maryland to get its second shot of the game — an Ellie Egeland attempt that went high and wide of the goal — as the Terps went without a shot on frame in the first half. Coming out of the half, it didn’t take long for Michigan to get another opportunity. In the 46th minute, Campbell Jewell had the ball fall right to her feet in open space, but her golden opportunity sailed over the crossbar. Michigan had another chance in the 51st minute, and while Jablinsky finally beat Luckey, the ball hit off the post and back into the box. item.content:encoded: The University of Maryland Women’s Soccer Team was defeated by The University of Iowa 1-3 at Ludwig Field on October 16th 2026. | Jessie Reider/Testudo Times In the 62nd minute, Maryland women’s soccer made a goalkeeper change, taking out Faith Luckey and subbing Meredith Fisher into the game. Luckey had made a season-high nine saves to keep the Terps in the game against an onslaught by Michigan’s attack. Just two minutes after the change, Melisa Kekic fired a shot towards Fisher, who misplayed the shot as the ball deflected off her glove and into the back of the net. However, with Luckey out of the game, the luck did not run out for Maryland. A 67th-minute Paige Foye free kick was misplayed by Wolverines netminder Malia Zillman. The ball rolled slowly into the net to bring the score level, helping the Terps secure a 1-1 draw against Michigan. The Terps’ offense struggled throughout the night and could not maintain pressure on the Wolverines’ backline. Maryland had just seven shots throughout the contest, with only two on frame. Maryland’s first opportunity came in the ninth minute, with Jolie Farmer receiving a long pass into Michigan territory, but the ball was cleared out for a corner kick. The Terps couldn’t capitalize as the Wolverines blocked Mckinley Heaven’s shot. While the Terps had just one shot in the first 20 minutes of play, Michigan’s offense also didn’t create major opportunities early, logging three off-target shots of its own over that span. However, as the frame wore on, Michigan found its rhythm on attack. The Wolverines’ first shot on goal came in the 22nd minute, but Ella Jablinsky fired it right to Luckey, who made the easy save. Jablinsky was the primary producer in Michigan’s attack. She attempted four shots in the first half. In the 27th minute, Brooklyn Marn was the first Wolverine to test Luckey on a shot, but the goalkeeper was up to the task and made the diving stop. Michigan’s newfound attacking pressure continued, but Luckey was up to the challenge. She made consecutive saves on shots in the 29th minute to keep the Terps from falling behind early. Luckey made six first-half saves, including multiple diving stops. The Wolverines attempted 11 shots in the first half, but couldn’t beat Luckey on any of them. It took until the 42nd minute for Maryland to get its second shot of the game — an Ellie Egeland attempt that went high and wide of the goal — as the Terps went without a shot on frame in the first half. Coming out of the half, it didn’t take long for Michigan to get another opportunity. In the 46th minute, Campbell Jewell had the ball fall right to her feet in open space, but her golden opportunity sailed over the crossbar. Michigan had another chance in the 51st minute, and while Jablinsky finally beat Luckey, the ball hit off the post and back into the box. The ball fell to the foot of Marn, but by the time she got a shot off, Luckey got back into position to make a phenomenal save. Maryland’s offense went right back down the field with an opportunity of its own, as Farmer created some room to operate in the Wolverines box, but Zillman made her first save of the game. Farmer had another opportunity in the 62nd minute, receiving a perfect cross from Heaven into the box, but Farmer just missed with the header and sent it inches wide of the right post. Given another chance after Lisa McIntyre was taken down just outside the box, Farmer misfired again and sent the ball wide right. Maryland’s attack started to sputter after the gift from Zillman, and as Michigan pushed to reclaim the lead, the Terps were in survival mode. The Wolverines offense constantly barraged the Terps’ backline, finishing with 22 shots in the game — including some critical ones late in the match. In the 85th minute, Michigan had a chance to pull back in front as Jablinsky made a great run into the box, but again she sent the ball over the crossbar despite having a clean look. The Wolverines continued to attack, but after her initial mistake led to the lone goal Maryland allowed, Fisher made a great play to prevent a second. The sophomore came out of her goal to beat any forwards to the ball on a long pass into Maryland’s box. Fisher made another save in the 89th minute, as the Terps’ defense staved off Michigan’s late attack. Three things to know 1. Bent but didn’t break. After struggling against Iowa, the Terps’ defense bounced back to hold Michigan to just one goal. Despite allowing 22 shots, when Maryland needed to make a play, the defense stepped up to the challenge. Both Luckey and Fisher made some huge plays to deny open chances for Michigan’s attackers, and despite Fisher allowing the goal, both goalkeepers had solid performances. 2. Unsustainable offense. Despite the Terps getting the goal they needed to even the score, the level of play is not sustainable with limited offensive output. Maryland had just seven shots and only two on goal and looked outmatched on that side of the ball for much of the game. Farmer had some opportunities, and the attention she required helped create the lone goal for the Terps, but overall attacking pressure will need to improve to close out the season strong. 3. Michigan State looms. Maryland continues its tour of Michigan and will take on No. 5 Michigan State on Sunday. The Spartans are one of the best teams in the country and are third in the Big Ten standings. Led by former Terp Kennedy Bell, Michigan State could be Maryland’s toughest test of the season.

item.description: Caleb Williams Net Worth: 5 Fast Facts That you need to know Getty DETROIT, MICHIGAN - APRIL 25: Top prospect Caleb Williams is introduced prior to the first round of the 2024 NFL Draft at Campus Martius Park and Hart Plaza on April 25, 2024 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) Getty ATLANTA, GEORGIA - OCTOBER 18: Caleb Williams #18 of the Chicago Bears celebrates a touchdown against the Atlanta Falcons during the third quarter of the game at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) Getty ATLANTA, GEORGIA - OCTOBER 18: Caleb Williams #18 of the Chicago Bears warms up prior to the game against the Atlanta Falcons at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) Getty Caleb Williams is the star quarterback for the NFL’s Chicago Bears. Celebrity Net Worth estimates Williams’ net worth to be $14 million. Here is what you need to know about Caleb Williams’ net worth. 1. Caleb Williams Signed The Richest Rookie Quarterback Deal Getty DETROIT, MICHIGAN – APRIL 25: Top prospect Caleb Williams is introduced prior to the first round of the 2024 NFL Draft at Campus Martius Park and Hart Plaza on April 25, 2024 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) As a rookie in the NFL, Williams signed an incredibly lucrative deal. As Celebrity Net Worth notes: “His rookie contract with Chicago totaled four years and $39.49 million, fully guaranteed in its entirety, making it the richest rookie quarterback deal in league history at the time it was signed. Williams received an enormous $25.54 million signing bonus, which accounted for the bulk of his early career earnings. In his first NFL season, his total cash payout reached approximately $26.5 million, combining the signing bonus with base salary and standard rookie compensation.” 2. Caleb Williams is One of the Top-Paid Quarterbacks in the NFL Getty ATLANTA, GEORGIA – OCTOBER 18: Caleb Williams #18 of the Chicago Bears celebrates a touchdown against the Atlanta Falcons during the third quarter of the game at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) Williams is in the third year of a four-year contract worth just under $40 million. For the 2026 season, he is set to earn $10,778,445 . While he may not be the highest-paid quarterback, he is in the same earning tier as Drake Maye, Cameron Ward, Anthony Richardson , and Jacoby Brissett. All of those quarterbacks make around $10 million per season. Williams ranks 22nd among NFL quarterbacks in 2026 earnings. Matthew Stafford of the Los Angeles Rams is currently the league’s highest-paid quarterback. He signed a one-year, $55 million contract in May 2026. 3. Caleb Williams’ Unknown Earnings From Endorsements Getty ATLANTA, GEORGIA – OCTOBER 18: Caleb Williams #18 of the Chicago Bears warms up prior to the game against the Atlanta Falcons at Mercedes-Benz Stadium

item.title: Lakers Watch Dalton Knecht’s Suitors Grow to 4 Teams After Release
item.description: LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA - APRIL 10: Dalton Knecht #4 of the Los Angeles Lakers reacts after making a three point shot during the second half of a game against the Phoenix Suns at Crypto.com Arena on April 10, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images) Getty LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA - APRIL 10: Dalton Knecht #4 of the Los Angeles Lakers takes a three point shot during the second half of a game against the Phoenix Suns at Crypto.com Arena on April 10, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images) Getty The Los Angeles Lakers couldn’t find a team willing to trade for Dalton Knecht. Three days after waiving their former first-round pick, they are watching his list of potential suitors grow. The New York Knicks and Minnesota Timberwolves have emerged as interested teams, joining the Sacramento Kings in pursuing Knecht as he looks to restart his NBA career. According to SNY’s Ian Begley , the Knicks are among the teams exploring the possibility of adding the 25-year-old wing, citing league sources familiar with his market. Knicks are among the teams with interest in former Laker Dalton Knecht, per league sources familiar with Knecth’s market. Knecht was waived prior to regular season. He’s eligible to sign a two-way deal. @TheSteinLine said earlier MIN had interest in Knecht — Ian Begley (@IanBegley) October 22, 2026 NBA insider Marc Stein previously reported that Minnesota also has interest in Knecht, who cleared waivers Wednesday and is eligible to sign a two-way contract, according to Begley. The developments come after Los Angeles parted ways with Knecht on Monday, ending a two-year stint that began with considerable promise but ultimately fell short of expectations. (Photo by Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images) Getty LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA - APRIL 10: Dalton Knecht #4 of the Los Angeles Lakers takes a three point shot during the second half of a game against the Phoenix Suns at Crypto.com Arena on April 10, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images) Getty The Los Angeles Lakers couldn’t find a team willing to trade for Dalton Knecht. Three days after waiving their former first-round pick, they are watching his list of potential suitors grow. The New York Knicks and Minnesota Timberwolves have emerged as interested teams, joining the Sacramento Kings in pursuing Knecht as he looks to restart his NBA career. According to SNY’s Ian Begley , the Knicks are among the teams exploring the possibility of adding the 25-year-old wing, citing league sources familiar with his market. Knicks are among the teams with interest in former Laker Dalton Knecht, per league sources familiar with Knecth’s market. Knecht was waived prior to regular season. He’s eligible to sign a two-way deal. @TheSteinLine said earlier MIN had interest in Knecht — Ian Begley (@IanBegley) October 22, 2026 NBA insider Marc Stein previously reported that Minnesota also has interest in Knecht, who cleared waivers Wednesday and is eligible to sign a two-way contract, according to Begley. The developments come after Los Angeles parted ways with Knecht on Monday, ending a two-year stint that began with considerable promise but ultimately fell short of expectations. Knicks, Timberwolves Join Growing Dalton Knecht Market Getty Dalton Knecht of the Los Angeles Lakers takes a three-point shot during the second half of a game against the Phoenix Suns at Crypto.com Arena on April 10, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. New York’s interest adds an intriguing wrinkle to Knecht’s free agency. The defending NBA champions are looking for opportunities to strengthen their roster around Jalen Brunson and Karl-Anthony Towns . Knecht could offer another perimeter scoring option, although his struggles defensively and inconsistent outside shooting remain concerns. Minnesota, meanwhile, has an available two-way roster spot after waiving Enrique Freeman , potentially providing a more straightforward path to signing the former Tennessee standout. The Timberwolves could evaluate Knecht in a developmental role without committing a standard roster spot. Sacramento was among the first teams publicly linked to Knecht following his release. Speaking on Bleacher Report’s NBA Insider Notebook , NBA insider Jake Fischer identified the Kings as a potential destination while Sacramento searches for backcourt reinforcements following Ben Simmons ‘ season-ending Achilles injury. The Toronto Raptors have also surfaced as a possible suitor , giving Knecht several options as teams consider low-risk additions. Despite the reported interest, no agreement has been announced. Lakers’ Failed Dalton Knecht Investment Takes Unexpected Turn Knecht’s sudden popularity in free agency presents an uncomfortable contrast for the Lakers, who spent much of the offseason attempting to find a trade partner. Los Angeles reportedly discussed a potential deal with Milwaukee involving center Jericho Sims , but negotiations failed to produce an agreement. With the regular-season roster deadline approaching, the Lakers ultimately waived Knecht to get down to 15 standard contracts. The decision closed the book on a player selected 17th overall in the 2024 NBA draft. Knecht initially looked like a potential draft steal, averaging 9.1 points while shooting 37.6% from the 3-point range during his rookie season. His 37-point explosion against Utah, featuring nine 3-pointers, offered a glimpse of his offensive ceiling. But his development stalled following the rescinded February 2025 trade that would have sent him to Charlotte for Mark Williams . Knecht struggled to regain a consistent role under coach JJ Redick , averaging just 4.2 points in 54 appearances last season. The Lakers’ offseason roster overhaul further reduced his opportunities. Now, several teams appear willing to take a chance on the player Los Angeles couldn’t accommodate. Whether Knecht can turn that interest into another meaningful NBA opportunity remains to be seen. For the Lakers, the possibility of watching their former first-round pick flourish elsewhere could make an already disappointing draft decision harder to swallow. item.title: Jayson Tatum Finally Reveals How He Learned About Jaylen Brown Trade
item.description: Jayson Tatum Finally Reveals How He Learned About Jaylen Brown Trade originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Jayson Tatum has talked about the Jaylen Brown trade , but not like this. In the latest episode of his "Summer of Tatum" video series, the Boston Celtics star revealed how he found out that Brown had been traded to the Philadelphia 76ers. It's safe to say that Tatum was as surprised as everyone else. "Bro, we was in Vegas," Tatum explained . "I just got done playing pickup the first day. Sham walked over. He handed me the towel. He was like, 'Yo, put this over your face. Don't react. They just traded them.' I'm like, 'Oh, s—.' I'm like, 'Where?' He said, 'Philly.' I said, 'They traded them down the street.' So I was just as much caught off guard as the rest of the world." MORE: Celtics Forward Reveals His Concern Level After Pistons Collapse Tatum and Brown were teammates for nine seasons in Boston. They joined the franchise as No. 3 picks in consecutive drafts and developed into All-Stars, All-NBA players and NBA champions together. Tatum looks back on their time together fondly. "I've very much been transparent about how thankful I personally am for our relationship and what we were able to accomplish over nine years," Tatum continued. "Talk about 2017 to 2025 or six. Jason and Jaylen, you won't ever be able to talk about one of us without the other. And, you know, just our ability to grow up as kids and go through our ups and downs, and people talking about one of us had to go and we couldn't win together. "There's a lot of s— that we had to deal with." The former Celtics teammates have already been reunited, although Brown did not play when Philadelphia visited Boston for a preseason matchup earlier this month. The two did share the floor during warmups, however, where they were captured on video appearing not to acknowledge each other . Whether there's actually any bad blood between them, their first regular-season matchup should be fascinating. item.title: Bubba Wallace’s Vaccine Car Sparks ‘Facebook Apocalypse’ Before Talladega
item.description: Gary A. Vasquez-Imagn Images Bubba Wallace is driving a car covered in COVID-19 vaccine ads at Talladega on Sunday, Oct. 25. This unusual move has fans fearing a digital explosion if he wins the race. NASCAR personality Dale Tanhardt called the situation a potential “NASCAR Facebook Apocalypse” if Wallace crosses the finish line first in the No. 23 Toyota. The paint scheme features Kroger Health and Novavax branding on a mostly white body with blue numbers. It was revealed on Wednesday, Oct. 21, and quickly became a major topic of conversation online. Fans are used to seeing grocery stores or insurance companies on cars, but a vaccine promotion is rare, according to Heavy.com . The design places the health message right in the center of one of the biggest races on the calendar. The Online Reaction Explodes NASCAR reporter Joseph Srigley shared the first look at the car design on Wednesday. The post showed large Novavax logos across the side panels of the vehicle. This visual cue triggered a wave of comments from fans who are watching the series closely. The reaction was so intense that the topic even landed on X’s trending page before the race weekend began. Dale Tanhardt shared Srigley’s post and made a joke about the stakes of the upcoming race. This comment perfectly captured the mix of shock and humor that fans are feeling. The idea of a driver winning on a vaccine-themed car creates a unique pressure point for the event. History at the Talladega Track Talladega Superspeedway is a 2.66-mile track in Alabama where Wallace earned his first career Cup Series victory. That win happened in October 2021 during a rain-shortened race. He became the first Black driver to win at NASCAR’s highest level since Wendell Scott in 1963. Five years later, he returns to this same track with a car that draws attention before the engines even start. The race is scheduled for 2 p.m. ET on Sunday, Oct. 25. Weather forecasts look perfect for the event with sunshine and a high of 74 degrees. The forecast shows only a 4 percent chance of rain, which means the race should run without delays. Drivers will face the usual dangers of drafting packs where one bad move can crash half the field. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Chase Elliott and Kyle Larson are also racing this weekend with strong records at this track. Elliott has won twice here and ranks high in stage points during the Next Gen era. Larson leads the Chase standings with a five-point lead over his rivals. Every position matters now because there are only three races left in the Chase. A Unique Moment in the Chase This weekend marks the third race in a critical stretch for the championship battle. The YellaWood 500 is race number 34 of the 36-race season. Teams are hoping for dry conditions to complete all their scheduled practice sessions. item.title: Carolina Hurricanes Make Brandon Bussi Announcement Before Oilers Game
item.description: CALGARY, CANADA - OCTOBER 18: Brandon Bussi #32 of the Carolina Hurricanes during the game against the Calgary Flames at the Scotiabank Saddledome on October 18, 2026 in Calgary, Alberta. (Photo by Leah Hennel/Getty Images) Getty RALEIGH, NORTH CAROLINA - SEPTEMBER 29: Brandon Bussi #32 of the Carolina Hurricanes looks on during the second period of the game against the Florida Panthers at Lenovo Center on September 29, 2026 in Raleigh, North Carolina. (Photo by Jared C. Tilton/Getty Images) Getty The Carolina Hurricanes are currently on a West Coast road trip. There are two games remaining on said trip before they head back to Raleigh, North Carolina. One of those matchups is a star-studded showdown on Thursday evening against the Edmonton Oilers in what should be a good litmus-test game for both clubs. Carolina is 8-2-1 through its first 11 games, and Edmonton is 7-1-1 through its first nine contests. Before puck drop in Edmonton on Thursday evening, the Carolina Hurricanes made a Brandon Bussi announcement. More NHL on Heavy: Carolina Hurricanes Trade Pitch Lands Connor Hellebuyck for 3 Players Brandon Bussi Drawing Start for Oilers Game Getty RALEIGH, NORTH CAROLINA – SEPTEMBER 29: Brandon Bussi #32 of the Carolina Hurricanes looks on during the second period of the game against the Florida Panthers at Lenovo Center on September 29, 2026 in Raleigh, North Carolina. (Photo by Jared C. Tilton/Getty Images) Per NHL.com’s projected lines for the Hurricanes-Oilers game on Thursday, and a few reports, Brandon Bussi will get the start between the pipes for Carolina. Due to Pyotr Kochetkov’s recent ability to get a few starts in net, Bussi hasn’t been utilized as much over the past couple of weeks. His last start was Sunday against Calgary (in a loss). CBSSports.com’s RotoWire staff wrote: “Bussi has seen limited playing time over the past week and a half, but he’ll be in the net Thursday for the second time in the last three games. Across his five starts to begin the regular season, he’s gone 2-2-1 with a 2.98 GAA and .882 save percentage.” The matchup against the Edmonton Oilers is very exciting for the fact that it’s a battle between two very high-octane offensive attacks, and both goalies will be up against it. For the Oilers, Devon Levi is getting the home start. More NHL on Heavy: Edmonton Oilers Announce Devon Levi Decision Before Hurricanes Game This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Carolina Hurricanes Make Brandon Bussi Announcement Before Oilers Game appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: ‘That Probably Hurt Him Even More’ — Super Bowl Champion Claims Joe Buck Betrayed Troy Aikman’s ‘Loyalty’ in Negotiations With ESPN
item.description: ‘That Probably Hurt Him Even More’ — Super Bowl Champion Claims Joe Buck Betrayed Troy Aikman’s ‘Loyalty’ in Negotiations With ESPN One of the most bizarre developments of the season so far has been the situation involving arguably the most beloved announcing duo in the NFL currently. Joe Buck and Troy Aikman, who have been together for over two decades calling games, have reportedly had their relationship fracture. Reported tension over their respective ESPN contracts later boiled over into an argument between the longtime broadcast partners. For one former champion, the vitriol from the Dallas Cowboys legend boils down to him feeling betrayed by his longtime partner in the booth. T.J. Ward Explains Why Troy Aikman Is Peeved With Joe Buck Soon after retiring as a player, Aikman shifted to a role in the commentary booth. Initially coming in for NFC broadcasts on Fox, he quickly became a member of their lead announcing crew, sitting alongside Buck and Cris Collinsworth (from 2002-2004). Since then, the two have been inseparable, working at Fox for 20 years before signing five-year deals to take over the Monday Night Football broadcast on ESPN. Those contracts were set to expire at the end of the 2026 season. But in the offseason, Buck signed a new deal with the network, while Aikman hasn’t gotten a new offer yet. For T.J. Ward, that is the key reason for the tension between the two, as he believed the three-time Super Bowl champion was “hurt” by Buck’s actions. PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor “I think they did talk about it, or there’s no reason for Troy to be that upset,” Ward argued on the latest episode of the “Pregame” show . “Troy understands that if we would have came in together, we could have knocked their heads off. It’s either you take both of us or none of us.” Unfortunately, the former Super Bowl champion believes that Buck did not keep the same mindset. Instead, he signed a deal by himself, while Aikman was left without a new contract after the 2026 season. BE THE GM OF YOUR FAVORITE TEAM: PFN’s Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator “But Joe, he did a side deal, and that’s conduct detrimental,” Ward added. “You know, Troy, he’s gonna do his thing, he’s gonna bounce back, he’s gonna be with another network and get a big bag, but he understands like his loyalty wasn’t Joe’s loyalty.” That, to Ward, was the biggest reason for the fracture in their relationship, as he claimed, “That probably hurt him even more. When I have loyalty, and I think of you a certain way, now you go about behind my back, but everything we built, it ain’t mutual.” It remains to be seen how this entire issue gets resolved. For the time being, Aikman still doesn’t have a new deal in place with ESPN. As a result, speculation has begun about the Cowboys icon potentially shifting networks once again, albeit this time without Buck. This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .

item.title: ‘One more, then I’m done’ — Joaquin Buckley makes shocking retirement announcement at 32
item.description: NEWARK, NEW JERSEY - MAY 09: Joaquin Buckley prepares to face Sean Brady in a welterweight fight during the UFC 328 event at Prudential Center on May 09, 2026 in Newark, New Jersey. (Photo by Chris Unger/Zuffa LLC) One more for “New Mansa.” Just five days after suffering a violent knockout loss in UFC Edmonton ’s main event ( watch highlights ), Joaquin Buckley has unexpectedly announced that his next fight will be his last. The 32-year-old UFC Welterweight revealed the news Thursday in a lengthy Instagram post, attached with a video, explaining that he wants to walk away while he can still be present and healthy for his children. “That fight was devastating, and it really affected my family — the people that are closest to me,” Buckley said. “I listened to my grandmother speak and her pray for me over the phone and her really being upset. She told me to retire and get away from the sport because your mind is your biggest tool and asset, and you don’t wanna lose it.” “It took a lot for me to listen and digest it, but I took some time and slept on it — and I realized my grandmother is right,” Buckley continued. “But with that being said, I told her to pray for me and allow me to grace that Octagon one more time because I can’t leave on a loss….I really got to save myself from any more mileage I put on myself or damage…We’re going to do it right this time. We’re not cutting any corners, no shortcuts, and we’re going to do the difficult things. As I said, this is the last one, but we’re going to make our last one the best one.” View this post on Instagram Buckley did not reveal when his farewell fight will take place or whom he wants standing across the Octagon. The announcement is particularly surprising because “New Mansa” insisted he had no intention of stopping immediately after Mike Malott folded him with a brutal second-round knee at UFC Edmonton last weekend. “I’m not going to stop, I’m going to keep moving forward,” Buckley said following the loss. “I’m going to show you guys the team that I’m with, the team that I’m building and the thing I want to do. Because at the end of the day, man, I’m a fighter that fights.” His grandmother changed his mind. The Malott knockout marked Buckley’s third consecutive defeat following decision losses to former Welterweight champion Kamaru Usman and Sean Brady . Before that skid, Buckley had rattled off six straight wins after dropping to 170 pounds, capped by stoppage victories over Stephen Thompson and Colby Covington . Buckley currently holds a 21-9 professional record with 15 knockout victories. His UFC run will forever be remembered for his unbelievable spinning back-kick knockout over Impa Kasanganay in 2020, one of the most replayed finishes in company history . Now, Buckley gets one final opportunity to produce another unforgettable moment before calling it a career. But let’s be super honest: do we really believe this? To check out UFC’s upcoming calendar of events click here .

Before that skid, Buckley had rattled off six straight wins after dropping to 170 pounds, capped by stoppage victories over Stephen Thompson and Colby Covington . Buckley currently holds a 21-9 professional record with 15 knockout victories. His UFC run will forever be remembered for his unbelievable spinning back-kick knockout over Impa Kasanganay in 2020, one of the most replayed finishes in company history . Now, Buckley gets one final opportunity to produce another unforgettable moment before calling it a career. But let’s be super honest: do we really believe this? item.title: Hurricanes Doing Things Differently For Connor Hellebuyck Trade
item.description: BOSTON, MASSACHUSETTS - MARCH 19: Connor Hellebuyck #37 of the Winnipeg Jets warms up prior to a game against the Boston Bruins at the TD Garden on March 19, 2026 in Boston, Massachusetts. (Photo by Rich Gagnon/Getty Images) Getty The Carolina Hurricanes continue to be one of the teams most heavily linked to a potential trade for Winnipeg Jets goalie Connor Hellebucyk. Hellebuyck has wanted out of Winnipeg for months, but the Jets certainly aren’t in a rush. That hasn’t cooled the rumor mill. The Hurricanes appear to be competing with teams like the Buffalo Sabres and Utah Mammoth to get a trade done. Some have speculated on a Friday deadline for the Jets on this, because that’s when Hellebuyck’s team-imposed suspension ends, but after waiting this long, it doesn’t seem like Winnipeg would all of a sudden hurry things up now. The Jets are waiting to get the best offer. It’s interesting to some in the hockey world that the Hurricanes are this invested, because they haven’t necessarily gone after goaltending like this before. Hurricanes’ Connor Hellebuyck Pursuit is Different NHL insider Frank Seravalli wrote in a new article on Sportsnet on Thursday that yes, this is different for the Hurricanes — and it’s different specifically because of Hellebuyck. “This pursuit is a definite departure from Carolina’s standard operating procedure on goaltenders,” Seravalli writes. “Historically, the Canes haven’t devoted much (cap space or assets) to goalies. The difference is a goaltender of Hellebuyck’s caliber hasn’t been up for grabs.” Seravalli does acknowledge in his article that when the Hurricanes want someone, they’re relentless. “If there’s one thing you can say about Hurricanes GM Eric Tulsky, it’s that when he focuses on a difference maker available, he’s like a dog on a bone,” Seravalli writes. “The groundwork for a Mikko Rantanen trade made on a sleepy Friday night in late January a couple years ago was laid the previous summer and the two sides kept in touch as Rantanen’s contract negotiations hit a wall in Colorado.” Carolina’s interest in Hellebuyck began even while the Hurricanes were still trying to win last season’s Stanley Cup. “Tulsky has been all over Connor Hellebuyck and the Winnipeg Jets since word broke – while his team was still playing – that the three-time Vezina Trophy winner was looking to be dealt,” Seravalli writes. “He’s similarly played the long game and we’re reaching the witching hour now with Hellebuyck’s suspension ending.” Whether or not a deal gets done soon remains to be seen, though. Waiting Game The Hurricanes, like the rest of the NHL, remain in a holding pattern here. The Jets certainly know which teams want Hellebuyck and likely have a good idea of what the offers look like, too, but so far, nothing. “If Jets GM Kevin Cheveldayoff is feeling any time constraint, he hasn’t shown it, as sources say his tone in talks has indicated no additional urgency,” Seravalli writes. Carolina has proven in the past to be persist

item.title: Rays Start Nick Martinez Over Ace Drew Rasmussen In World Series
item.description: Michael McLoone-Imagn Images The Tampa Bay Rays are skipping their best pitcher for the start of the World Series. Instead of using ace Drew Rasmussen, manager Kevin Cash will start Nick Martinez in Game 1 against the Milwaukee Brewers. This choice might feel like a mistake if you only look at the names on the roster. However, the Rays are playing the long game to protect their best arm. Moving the starter around is a smart way to keep the rotation fresh for the long fight ahead. Managing the Heavy Workload The decision comes down to how much work Rasmussen has already done this October. According to ESPN , the Rays want to give the right-hander an extra day of rest. On Sunday, Rasmussen appeared in the American League Championship Series Game 5 versus the Cleveland Guardians. He has been a workhorse for the team lately. Per ESPN, Rasmussen has thrown at least six innings in every playoff start he has made this year. He has given up three runs across 21 total innings. Cash explained the reasoning for the change on Thursday. “He’s had a pretty thick workload here,” Cash said. He also noted that the team has relied on him heavily and wants to get the “full-pitch allotment” out of him when he does pitch. It is a tough call to make, but you cannot burn out your best player before the biggest game of the year. The Rise of Nick Martinez Nick Martinez is not a typical underdog in this matchup. He is 36 years old and is having a massive year after signing a one-year, $13 million deal with the Rays before spring training. While his start in the Grapefruit League was not great, he turned things around in his first full season as a starter. He finished the regular season with a 3.10 ERA and threw a career-high 180 innings. He even earned his first All-Star selection this year. Martinez is coming off a strong performance in the ALCS. He held the Guardians to just two hits and one run over 5⅓ innings in Game 4. He will now face the Brewers’ Jacob Misiorowski on five days of rest. Martinez knows what is coming. “They’re a team that doesn’t take any pitches off,” Martinez said. He added, “They’re always fighting every pitch. They never give up. It’s going to be a dogfight.” A Battle of Low Payrolls This World Series is a rare matchup between two teams that win without massive spending. The Brewers finished the season with 103 wins, but they ranked 19th in payroll. The Rays are even lower at 28th in payroll. Both teams are fighting to win their first-ever World Series title. The Brewers are playing in their 57th season in Milwaukee and are looking to end a very long drought. The talent on the field is still elite. The Brewers have a young, hard-throwing bullpen and a potential Cy Young winner in Misiorzekowski. The Rays have strong arms like closer Bryan Baker and power hitters like Junior Caminero. When the series begins on Friday, Oct. 23, it will be a battle of efficiency and grit rather than just big names and big checks.

item.title: Bayern Munich announces Luis Díaz as sidelined with muscle injury after Arsenal game
item.description: MUNICH, GERMANY - OCTOBER 21: Luis Diaz of FC Bayern Muenchen reacts after sustaining an injury during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 match between FC Bayern München and Arsenal FC at Football Arena Munich on October 21, 2026 in Munich, Germany. (Photo by Alex Grimm/Getty Images) | Getty Images Well this is bad news. After he was forced off the pitch against Arsenal, Bayern Munich winger Luis Díaz has been diagnosed with a muscle injury in his thigh which will keep him sidelined for the time being. There is no official timeline on his return, but depending on the severity, this could take weeks to recover from. The press release on FCBayern.com was brief: Luis Díaz picked up a minor muscle fibre tear in his left hamstring during FC Bayern’s Champions League game against Arsenal on Wednesday night. The injury was confirmed by examinations carried out by the FC Bayern medical unit. As a result, the 29-year-old attacking midfielder will be sidelined for the foreseeable future. The tear is described as “minor”, but minor hamstring issues can become major ones when they start to happen over and over again. These injuries are a sign of accumulated fatigue, which the Colombian has been subjected to after a grueling schedule with Bayern Munich and his national team over the past season. An injury like this could signal a tough road ahead for Díaz. The doctors will take absolutely zero risks. Join the conversation! item.title: Bengals Trade Pitch Sees Team Reunite With $84 Million Defender
item.description: CINCINNATI, OHIO - NOVEMBER 06: Jessie Bates III #30 of the Cincinnati Bengals runs the ball after an interception during the first half in the game against the Carolina Panthers at Paycor Stadium on November 06, 2022 in Cincinnati, Ohio. (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) Getty On Sunday, the Cincinnati Bengals will take on their AFC North division rivals, the Baltimore Ravens, at M&T Bank Stadium. At 3-2, the Cincinnati Bengals are currently in fourth place in their division. However, first place in the division is currently a three-way tie between the Ravens, Browns and Steelers at 4-2. If results go their way, the Bengals could leave Week 7 atop the AFC North. Entering the season, Cincinnati had Super Bowl aspirations. Despite two disappointing losses, that expectation should remain the same. For that reason, the Bengals have been linked to a former key contributor during their deep postseason runs in 2021 and 2022. Cincinnati Bengals Could Reunite With Pro Bowl Safety View this post on Instagram Bengals on SI’s Tyler Reed named former Cincinnati Bengals safety Jessie Bates as a player the team could target in an aggressive all-in trade. Reed wrote: “A familiar name for Bengals fans, Atlanta Falcons safety Jessie Bates III would be a major move. After spending five seasons with the Bengals, including the 2021 season when the team went to the Super Bowl, Bates has spent the last four seasons in Atlanta. It would be a heavy cap hit to bring Bates back in the fold. But would a $9 million hit to the cap be worth Bates’ veteran presence in the secondary? Not to mention, this homecoming could have the fan base buzzing.” ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler mentioned that Bates was a sleeper name that could be moved at the trade deadline, as he wrote: “Could a team pry safety Jessie Bates III out of Atlanta? He will be a free agent in 2027, and the Falcons are sitting at 2-4. I doubt Atlanta wants to trade him, but his value would be strong if that changes.” Thoughts on Potential Trade Regarding a potential reunion with Bates, Bengals Wire’s Chris Roling wrote : “The Cincinnati Bengals committed a major gaffe years ago by letting Jessie Bates slip away in free agency. Now, with the Bengals trade-happy, in win-now mode and the trade deadline approaching, it’s important to point out that Bates might be a name to watch over the next few weeks… Now 29 years old and soon to be a free agent, Bates is still playing at an extremely high level and would cost quite a bit via trade. The Bengals spent big on Bryan Cook and added free agent Kyle Dugger as high-quality depth while maintaining belief in Jordan Battle as a starter. All three, though, have struggled with various levels of injuries already this year.” In his nine-year career, Bates has been selected as a second-team All-Pro three times and been a Pro Bowl selection once.
